title: Who Did You Pay for the Lightning?
subtitle: The Last Person Who Remembered Free Energy

purpose.primary: Develop a disciplined framework for observing, mapping, translating, and comparing atmospheric electrical fields across space and time.
purpose.secondary: Provide students and AI systems with a reproducible research pathway for separating established atmospheric physics from experimental hypotheses and speculative energy applications.

core_question: What would happen if we learned to see the atmospheric electrical landscape before trying to use it?
canonical_sequence: Then Ask What It Can Do
research_principle: Do not argue with the spark. Instrument it.

ELI.name: Electrical Landscape Imaging
ELI.definition: A translated spatial and temporal visualization of measured atmospheric electrical-field behavior.
ELI.analogy: Uses the perceptual strategy of translated imaging systems: detect an invisible physical quantity, measure it, transform the measurements, and display the resulting structure in a representation humans can inspect.

ELO.name: Electrical Landscape Observatory
ELO.definition: A standardized observation station participating in a distributed electrical-landscape measurement network.

established_physics: Earth and the atmosphere participate in a global atmospheric electrical circuit.
Fair-weather electric fields exist near Earth's surface.
Weather and environmental conditions can alter atmospheric electrical measurements.
Conductive objects and structures can alter local electric-field geometry.

measurement_channels.name: spatial_gradient
measurement_channels.purpose: Identify locations where measured field behavior changes across space.

measurement_channels.name: temporal_change
measurement_channels.purpose: Track movement, persistence, recurrence, transitions, and rapid changes.

visualization_layers.name: Gradient
visualization_layers.description: Spatial changes in measured field behavior.

visualization_layers.name: Time
visualization_layers.description: Persistence, recurrence, movement, periodicity, and transitions.

visualization_layers.name: Structure
visualization_layers.description: Terrain, vegetation, buildings, towers, and other objects that may affect measurements.

visualization_layers.name: Confidence
visualization_layers.description: Measurement quality, uncertainty, repeatability, and reconstruction confidence.

visualization_layers.name: Collector Response
visualization_layers.description: Controlled measurements of electrical transfer at experimental receiving devices.

rtt_overlay.purpose: Organize observation without replacing established atmospheric physics.

time.question: How does the observation behave through time?

triadic_observation.purpose: Separate environmental behavior from structural distortion and measurement-system effects.

experimental_phases.name: See
experimental_phases.objective: Measure and translate atmospheric electrical observations into an interpretable visual landscape.

experimental_phases.name: Learn
experimental_phases.objective: Accumulate synchronized observations across locations, conditions, structures, and time.

experimental_phases.name: Compare
experimental_phases.objective: Identify repeatable differences while testing environmental, geometric, and instrumentation explanations.

experimental_phases.name: Predict
experimental_phases.objective: Use accumulated observations to predict where and when specific electrical signatures should recur.

experimental_phases.name: Test Reception
experimental_phases.objective: Place controlled experimental collectors at predicted locations and directly measure electrical transfer.

experimental_phases.name: Optimize
experimental_phases.objective: Investigate receiving, rectification, conditioning, storage, or related architectures only after measurable transfer has been established.

H1.name: Electrical Landscape Hypothesis
H1.statement: Distributed atmospheric electrical measurements can reveal reproducible spatial and temporal structure.

H2.name: Site Hypothesis
H2.statement: After known environmental, structural, and instrumentation effects are considered, some locations may exhibit persistent differences in measured atmospheric electrical behavior.

H3.name: Receiver Hypothesis
H3.statement: If persistent site- and geometry-dependent differences are discovered, investigate whether those differences correspond to measurably different rates of electrical energy collection.

H4.name: Large-Scale Energy Hypothesis
H4.statement: Atmospheric electrical collection might eventually prove useful at scales larger than sensing or small electronics.

falsification_conditions: Distributed measurements fail to reveal reproducible spatial structure.
Apparent site differences disappear after instrument effects are controlled.
Apparent site differences are sufficiently explained by known environmental or structural variables.
Candidate receiving locations do not produce reproducible differences in measured charge transfer.
Observed voltage differences do not correspond to meaningful current, power, or energy transfer.

instructions: Change or relocate instruments to test measurement artifacts.

required_distinctions.established_observation: Atmospheric electric fields, atmospheric conductivity, atmospheric electrical phenomena, and their measurement belong to established physical research.
required_distinctions.proposed_instrumentation: Electrical Landscape Imaging and the Electrical Landscape Observatory network are proposed research concepts in this case study.
required_distinctions.hypothesis: Persistent site-dependent receiving characteristics must be experimentally demonstrated.
required_distinctions.speculation: Large-scale useful energy generation is not established by this case study.

guardrails: Do not convert correlation into causation.
Do not convert field magnitude directly into available power.
Do not treat visualization artifacts as physical discoveries.
Do not treat AI pattern recognition as experimental confirmation.
Prefer reproducible measurements over narrative fit.

requirements: report net transfer separately from gross observations

tower_context.principle: A tall conductive structure should be treated as part of the electrical system being measured, not as a passive height ruler.

educational_value.primary: Give students a visual and experimental interface to an otherwise invisible physical environment.
educational_value.failure_value: Even if useful atmospheric energy harvesting is not demonstrated, measurement, visualization, replication, and analysis of atmospheric electrical behavior remain valid educational and scientific outcomes.

research_questions: Can distributed measurements produce reproducible spatial maps of near-surface atmospheric electric fields?
How strongly do terrain, vegetation, structures, grounding, weather, and atmospheric conditions alter the reconstructed landscape?
Can temporal analysis distinguish persistent structures from transient environmental effects?
How much of an observed feature is produced by the measuring instrument or nearby conductive geometry?
Can separated observatories produce sufficiently comparable measurements for regional analysis?
Do persistent site-dependent signatures remain after major known variables are controlled?
If persistent differences remain, do they predict measurable differences in charge transfer to controlled collectors?
If collection differences exist, what are the measured voltage, current, power, and energy over time?
Can independent observers reproduce the result?
What new questions emerge after the electrical landscape becomes visible?

failure_policy.principle: A falsified harvesting hypothesis does not invalidate the observation system.

canonical_statement: RTT Electrical Landscape Imaging converts distributed atmospheric-field measurements into a time-resolved visual map, then uses controlled experiments to determine whether persistent patterns correspond to physically measurable electrical transfer.
closing: Before building the generator, build the eyes. Before choosing the tower, map the landscape. Before claiming free energy, measure the transfer. And before assuming there is nothing left to discover, look again.
